title: In Silico Modeling Method for Computational Aquatic Toxicology of Endocrine Disruptors: A Software-Based Approach Using QSAR Toolbox
protocol: Upon starting the QSAR Toolbox, begin at the Input toolbox stage by default.
Rename the working file "Document 1" by right-clicking if desired.
Click on the CAS# button in the actions toolbar and enter the chemical abstract service (CAS) number of the target substance.
Click Search to initiate the search for the target substance by CAS number.
Choose other available search options such as searching by substance name or SMILES code, clicking Name or Structure accordingly.
Use the Structure tool to draw the target substance if necessary.
Select the record reporting a "high" CAS-SMILES relation when multiple records are retrieved and click OK.
Write a simple substance list in a text editor with each CAS number listed in a single row.
Save the text file with an appropriate name and extension .txt on the computer.
Click Data, then go to Databases in the stage option panel on the left.
Make sure databases that are listed under Ecotoxicological Information are checked.
Click Input, select Query from the actions toolbar, and accept settings by clicking Yes.
Choose the CAS tab and upload the substance list through Load list from your computer.
Click the Add button at the bottom of the pop-up menu, then click Execute.
Run integrated 2D and 3D QSAR models available in the QSAR Toolbox by right-clicking Parameter in the endpoint tree.
Click Calculate/extract all parameters for all chemicals in the pop-up menu.
Use “Profiling methods” for qualitative information (see step 2.3.1).
Gather experimental data from the Data stage button and Actions toolbar.
Select All endpoints to gather all experimental data, then choose specific endpoint data as needed.
If focusing on aquatic toxicity, click Choose > Ecotoxicological Information > Aquatic toxicity > OK.
Organize the endpoint tree in the preferred manner by right-clicking the endpoint of interest and choosing Set tree hierarchy.
Export gathered data as an Excel file by right-clicking on the endpoint of interest and selecting Export Data matrix.
Open the “Matrix export” wizard and add other endpoints to the export list.
Click Export and save the file on the computer.
Click on the toolbox stage button Data gap filling.
Click Automated in the Actions toolbar.
Select Ecotoxicological Endpoint > Fish, LC50 (lethal concentration, 50%) at 96 h for Pimephales promelas (mortality).
Click OK to start data processing which may take several minutes.
Close the workflow controller after receiving a message indicating “Finished workflow” by clicking x in the upper right corner.
Upon starting the automated workflow, specify the range of substances for execution by default.
Close the workflow controller indicating “Finished workflow” at the end of batch processing by clicking x in the upper right corner.
Do not generate reports in batch mode.
Scroll down and find the prediction value in matrix field located in a yellow highlighted row next to endpoint “96-h.”
Activate the specific data matrix field by left-clicking it.
Click Prediction in the Actions toolbar.
Customize report content and appearance in the pop-up wizard.
Include author’s name and contact details if desired.
Write a short summary for the mechanistic interpretation or justification of prediction adequacy.
Provide additional information related to executed prediction as needed.
